acceptance.criterion: Truncated/tampered DB/bundle/manifest, duplicate/omitted/unknown brain, unsupported schema and unsafe path all fail before reactivation.
acceptance.expected: Every listed corruption/tamper class is rejected before any bytes are published to the restore destination.
acceptance.observed: Fixture tests cover: truncated/tampered control.db and bundle (checksum/length), truncated and legacy-v1 manifest, tampered bundle head recorded in the manifest, unknown brain (renamed ID) and omitted brain (dropped manifest entry) against the restored control database, a ready brain tampered into a false manifest Empty claim (TestRestoreRejectsReadyBrainMarkedEmptyInManifest -- reproduces a real data-loss path the coordinator demonstrated: a structurally valid manifest keeping a ready brain's ID but zeroing its artifact/heads and setting Empty=true previously passed inventory verification and restoreBrain silently created an empty directory in its place; confirmed this test fails against the prior code and passes against the fix), schema-version mismatch between manifest and artifact (checked read-only before store.Open can migrate), and a symlinked control.db/bundle/manifest.json. Every case leaves no destination directory at all (os.Stat confirms ErrNotExist). Fixture/local-process evidence only. TestRestoreRejectsDuplicateInventoryAndUnsafePaths explicitly rejects duplicate brain IDs, control/bundle parent traversal, absolute control paths and nested bundle paths through Restore with ErrManifestInvalid and no destination publication.

acceptance.criterion: Manifest roundtrip matches exact fact IDs and canonical bundle heads; restored raw credentials/sessions remain invalid.
acceptance.expected: A create-then-restore round trip reproduces identical canonical content and exact bundle heads (including the bundle's own HEAD entry), and restored client_credentials/sessions/oauth_* state is revoked or cleared.
acceptance.observed: TestCreateRestoreRoundTripPreservesCanonicalMemoryFact drives the product's real internal/writer.MemoryFact write path (backed by internal/store.SourceStore, the same store.LoadMemoryProjection a live read path uses) and proves the restored brain projects the identical content-addressed fact ID (SHA256) with byte-identical payload (fact text, provenance, entity slug, kind, visibility, created_at) -- not a brain.txt proxy. TestCreateRestoreRoundTrip and TestRoundTripPreservesEveryBranchAndTag verify exact manifest/bundle heads including multiple branches and a tag are restored as real local refs, not left as refs/remotes/origin/* tracking refs. TestRestoreRevokesCredentialsAndOAuthState seeds one row each of oauth_grants (plus its cascade-owned oauth_tokens/oauth_refresh), oauth_codes, oauth_consents, sessions, login_tokens and a client_credentials row, then asserts all seven tables are fully cleared/revoked after restore, not just client_credentials. All fixture/local-process evidence; no live service/gateway process was run.

acceptance.criterion: Live write during coordinated backup is either included consistently or excluded as a later operation; no acknowledged pre-snapshot write lost.
acceptance.expected: A write present when Create runs is either included in the snapshot consistently, or Create fails in a way that provably loses nothing, deferring the write to a subsequent, successful backup.
acceptance.observed: Per coordinator review, Create no longer flushes a dirty canonical tree into an extra commit of its own (that risked sweeping unrelated/unreviewed files into canonical history); it now only ever runs a read-only `git status --porcelain` check and fails closed on any dirty brain. TestCreateRefusesDirtyCanonicalState proves this refusal is lossless and side-effect-free: after a failed Create, the source file's bytes, the git index bytes, HEAD, and the working tree's dirty-status output are all asserted byte-for-byte unchanged, and no destination is published. This is real coverage of one sub-case (a write already dirty when Create starts is never silently lost -- it is refused and left exactly as-is for a later, successful backup after a flush), and it proves live Service.Backup's existing Pool.FlushAll-before-Create sequencing is load-bearing (documented in integration-request.md). It does NOT exercise a genuinely concurrent writer racing with an in-progress `git bundle` call during the backup window -- that requires a live service/gateway process and is explicitly out of scope for this fixture-level lane. The schema's acceptance-status enum has no PARTIAL value; this criterion's full 'assembled, concurrent acknowledged write' scope is recorded NOT_RUN rather than overstated as PASS, notwithstanding the real lossless-refusal sub-case above.

No genuinely concurrent writer racing with an in-progress bundle/backup was exercised; only a write already dirty when Create starts is covered, and only via provably lossless refusal, not inclusion.

Create's bundle files and Restore's cloned brain repository trees are now explicitly fsynced (bottom-up for directories) before publication, closing a gap where fsyncDir(staging) alone only covered staging's own directory entries, not nested file/directory durability. Source inspection confirms explicit sync calls and error propagation; the full staging tree now includes intermediate parent directories. Passing roundtrip tests do not prove crash consistency or injected sync-error handling; those qualifications remain unrun.
